identity.title: Runner help exits with usage failure code

origin.summary: The developer guide previously recommended Runner --help, but direct execution showed that help is treated as invalid usage.

state.current_summary: The missing explicit help route caused --help to fall through to invalid usage. RunnerCommandRouter now routes case-insensitive help through the shared usage writer to stdout with exit 0, while missing and unknown commands retain the same usage on stderr with exit 2; Release and existing Runner regression checks pass.

claims.text: OpenVisionLab.ThreeD.Runner --help prints usage but exits with code 2 instead of a successful help exit.

problem.impact: Scripts, users, and documentation checks cannot distinguish a successful request for help from an invalid command.

criteria.text: --help and a case-insensitive equivalent print usage and exit 0.
Missing required values and unknown command combinations continue to exit nonzero with controlled usage output.

context.summary: The final recipe/report validation prints the shared usage block and returns 2; no explicit help branch was found.

artifacts.summary: Runner binary used for the direct --help exit-code observation.

evidence.observation: The current Release Runner printed its usage text and returned exit code 2.

Release Runner --help and --HELP each wrote the shared 4004-byte usage body to stdout, wrote zero bytes to stderr, and exited 0; both usage bodies have SHA-256 CEFCB5D382309FC56DD9053EBE63CADFCC25242602983CCCD646D8CDAF87B2FC.
An unknown command and a recipe command missing --report each wrote zero bytes to stdout, wrote the same shared usage body to stderr, and exited 2; both usage bodies match E2's SHA-256.

events.summary: Added an explicit case-insensitive help success route while preserving controlled nonzero invalid and incomplete command exits.
